tool.name: Define haplotype windows
tool.description: size read-level haplotype windows from the fragment-length distribution of a cohort
tool.command: ## Windows must be identical across every specimen or the resulting sheets have ## non-corresponding columns, so this is a COHORT-level reduction over the BAM ## collection, deliberately not a per-specimen step. mkdir -p bams && #for $i, $b in enumerate($bams) ln -s '$b' 'bams/${i}.bam' && ln -s '${b.metadata.bam_index}' 'bams/${i}.bam.bai' && #end for pyeuk define-windows --ref '$ref' --bams bams/*.bam --sample $sample --min-spanning $min_spanning #if str($legacy_spanning_target).strip() != '' --spanning-target $legacy_spanning_target #end if --min-depth $min_depth --window-min $window_min --window-max $window_max --width-step $width_step #if int($step) > 0 --step $step #end if --out '$windows'

param.name: bams
param.label: Aligned BAMs (the cohort)
param.help: A collection or several datasets. A sample of these is scanned; all of them get the same windows.

param.name: ref
param.label: Reference the BAMs were aligned to

param.name: min_spanning
param.label: Minimum MEASURED fraction of reads that span a window
param.help: The widest candidate width at which at least this fraction of the reads OVERLAPPING a window actually cover it end to end. Measured per reference contig from the BAMs, not inferred. The rule it replaced took a read-length percentile and delivered 30-33% spanning while reporting 70%: read length is not spanning, because a read only spans a window if it also starts early enough.

param.name: legacy_spanning_target
param.label: Legacy percentile rule (leave EMPTY)
param.help: DEPRECATED. Set a value here only to reproduce a pre-2026-08 run exactly. Any value overrides the measured rule above and restores the read-length percentile behaviour.

param.name: min_depth
param.label: Depth for a position to count as covered

param.name: window_max
param.label: Maximum window length (0 = no cap)
param.help: THE parameter to check per panel. Long windows carry more linkage but accumulate sequencing error and shatter into singletons, which pushes minor haplotypes below the frequency gate. Measured on a Cryptosporidium mixture titration: at 250 bp a pure control matched its own string in 62% of reads and both 75:25 mixtures were called as a single haplotype; at 100 bp the control reached 79% and every mixture was resolved.

tool.help:
Derives a window BED for a cohort, from the reads themselves. Two things are measured, both panel- and species-agnostic:
**size** -- the aligned block length distribution, per reference sequence. Amplicons differ in depth and fragment length, so one cohort-wide size is set by whichever amplicon is deepest and is then far too wide for the shallow ones. Sizing is therefore per reference sequence.
**extent** -- the positions reads actually reach. Amplicon reads start inside the primer, so tiling from position 1 wastes the first window on sequence nothing spans.
